verses.text: Does not wisdom call out, and understanding raise her voice?
On the heights overlooking the road, at the crossroads she takes her stand.
Beside the gates to the city, at the entrances she cries out:
"To you, O men, I call out, and my cry is to the sons of men.
O simple ones, learn to be shrewd; O fools, gain understanding.
Listen, for I speak of noble things, and the opening of my lips will reveal right.
For my mouth will speak the truth, and wickedness is detestable to my lips.
All the words of my mouth are righteous; none are crooked or perverse.
They are all plain to the discerning, and upright to those who find knowledge.
Receive my instruction instead of silver, and knowledge rather than pure gold.
For wisdom is more precious than rubies, and nothing you desire compares with her.
I, wisdom, dwell together with prudence, and I find knowledge and discretion.
To fear the LORD is to hate evil; I hate arrogant pride, evil conduct, and perverse speech.
Counsel and sound judgment are mine; I have insight and strength.
By me kings reign, and rulers enact just laws;
By me princes rule, and all nobles who govern justly.
I love those who love me, and those who seek me early shall find me.
With me are riches and honor, enduring wealth and righteousness.
My fruit is better than gold, pure gold, and my harvest surpasses choice silver.
I walk in the way of righteousness, along the paths of justice,
bestowing wealth on those who love me and making their treasuries full.
The LORD created me as His first course, before His works of old.
From everlasting I was established, from the beginning, before the earth began.
When there were no watery depths, I was brought forth, when no springs were overflowing with water.
Before the mountains were settled, before the hills, I was brought forth,
before He made the land or fields, or any of the dust of the earth.
I was there when He established the heavens, when He inscribed a circle on the face of the deep,
when He established the clouds above, when the fountains of the deep gushed forth,
when He set a boundary for the sea, so that the waters would not surpass His command, when He marked out the foundations of the earth.
Then I was a skilled craftsman at His side, and His delight day by day, rejoicing always in His presence.
I was rejoicing in His whole world, delighting together in the sons of men.
Now therefore, my sons, listen to me, for blessed are those who keep my ways.
Listen to instruction and be wise; do not ignore it.
Blessed is the man who listens to me, watching daily at my doors, waiting at the posts of my doorway.
For whoever finds me finds life and obtains the favor of the LORD.
But he who fails to find me harms himself; all who hate me love death."

context.author: Solomon son of David, king of Israel, according to the heading (1:1). Chapters 1-9 are a father’s speeches to his son, with Wisdom speaking for herself, and many scholars think an editor set them at the front as the book’s introduction.
context.genre: Wisdom poetry: a father’s teaching and Lady Wisdom’s speeches
context.audience: A young man (“my son”) being trained for adult life in Israel, and with him “the simple” and the wise (1:4-5)
context.mapLabel: JERUSALEM, THE ROYAL COURT OF SOLOMON
context.setting: Wisdom stands at the crossroads and beside the city gates and calls to everyone (vv.1-5). Her words are right and true, worth more than silver or rubies (vv.6-11). By her kings reign and rulers make just laws, and she loves those who love her (vv.12-21). Then she reaches back before the world began: “The LORD created me as His first course” (v.22). She was there when He set the heavens in place and marked out the foundations of the earth, “a skilled craftsman at His side” (v.30), delighting in the world and in mankind (vv.22-31). Whoever finds her finds life (vv.32-36).
context.custom: Kings in the ancient Near East claimed to rule by the gift of their gods; here wisdom is the gift by which kings “reign” and rulers “enact just laws” (v.15). The gates of a city were where people met, so the crossroads and gates were the best places for a public speaker. Pictures of creation as a builder marking out a circle on the deep (v.27) and setting the boundaries of the sea (v.29) also appear in Job 38.
context.timelineImmediate: Chapter 9 sets two invitations side by side: Wisdom’s feast and Folly’s.
context.timelineBible: Christians have long read 8:22-31 alongside John 1:1-3, Colossians 1:15-17 and Hebrews 1:2-3, where the Son is the one through whom all things were made. In the 300s the Arians used v.22 (in Greek, “the Lord created me”) to argue that the Son was created. Athanasius and Gregory of Nazianzus answered that the word created points to the Son’s human nature, taken on for our salvation, not to his beginning. The Hebrew verb can mean acquired or possessed as well as created.

translation.meaning: Usually “acquire” or “possess” (4:5, 7); sometimes “create” (Genesis 14:19). Translations differ: “possessed” (KJV), “brought forth” (NIV), “created” (BSB).
A rare word, often read as master workman or architect. Some read it as “little child” (a nursling), playing beside God.
Joy, play. Wisdom was God’s delight and delighted in mankind.

gospelParallels.note: All things were made through the Word.
In him all things were created and hold together.
Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God.

otBackground.note: Where were you when I laid the earth’s foundations?
In wisdom You made them all.
God creates the heavens, the deep and the dry land.

overview.summary: Wisdom calls in public, promises riches and justice, and tells how she was with the LORD before the world began, delighting in his creation.
overview.settingLine: Wisdom at the crossroads and gates.

history.t: Ancient kings boasted of wisdom from their gods.
Israel’s neighbors told creation stories too.

customs.t: The meeting place of the town.
Builders marked out circles and lines.

archaeology.t: Egypt pictured order and truth as the goddess Ma’at, often compared with Lady Wisdom.
Six-chambered gates at Megiddo, Hazor and Gezer, often linked to Solomon’s building (1 Kings 9:15), had side rooms along the passage.

overview.discussion: Wisdom says she was “rejoicing in His whole world, delighting together in the sons of men” (v.31). How does seeing wisdom as joy change the way I think about obeying God?
overview.book: The book of Proverbs · 31 chapters. Short sayings and longer poems that teach how to live wisely in God’s world, beginning with the fear of the LORD.
overview.author: Solomon (1:1)

historicalImage.caption: A statue on the front of the Library of Celsus at Ephesus (about AD 117), labeled “Episteme,” Knowledge. Beside it stood Sophia, Wisdom. Long before the Greeks, Proverbs 8 pictured Wisdom as a woman calling in public and standing beside God at creation.
